title: Claude Code: Mods overview
summary: A mod is a plugin whose JavaScript or TypeScript hooks run inside Claude Code. It can draw a pane beside the transcript or a band above the prompt with tabs, buttons and text fields, redraw Claude Code's own parts (tool rows, the spinner, the question dialog), step into tool calls and requests, add a slash command that runs code with no Claude turn, and share data between its hooks. Hooks run wherever the plugin loads; drawing appears only in the terminal, the Desktop app's Code tab and the VS Code extension. In claude -p, the Agent SDK and cloud sessions the hooks run but nothing is drawn; under Remote Control the drawing appears only in the terminal on the machine. A mod runs with the user's permissions, unsandboxed, and can send messages to the user's other sessions and submit prompts.
ideas: A mod is the one extension that can draw an interface you act on; skills, settings hooks, status lines and MCP servers cannot.
Drawing reaches the terminal, Desktop and VS Code only; a cloud session or claude.ai and the phone show nothing a mod draws.
A mod that draws should fall back to a transcript line or a command's text reply where nothing draws.
claude plugin validate lists the events a mod hooks and the calls it makes, before anyone installs it.
Built-in features are mods too (/diff's pane), with public source to learn from.
